### Expected Behavior

The native resize hit-test area should be limited to the actual outer edge of the window.

When `titleBarStyle` is changed from `"default"` to `"hidden"`, the resize border should not move inward into the visible client/content area.

A pointer position that is treated as normal client content with `titleBarStyle: "default"` should remain normal client content with `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` if it is visually inside the window and not on the outer border.

### Actual Behavior

With `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` on Windows, the native resize hit-test area extends into the visible client/content area.

The mouse cursor changes to a horizontal resize cursor while the pointer is still visually inside the application window, not on the actual outer border.

The same visual pointer position does not trigger resize behavior when using `titleBarStyle: "default"`.

This happens without any custom CSS drag regions or custom titlebar implementation, so the issue appears to be in Electron's Windows native hit-testing / non-client area calculation for hidden-titlebar windows.
